exposure: intraspinal nerve block anesthesia for labor
cohort: 90 eligible primiparous women enrolled for delivery in an obstetrics and gynecology department.
finding: Intraspinal nerve block anesthesia effectively reduced labor pain but was associated with higher intrapartum body temperature and more cases of fever, though no adverse consequences for newborns were observed.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences in the delivery mode between women who received intraspinal nerve block anesthesia and those who did not.
followup_time: At birth/intrapartum for neonates, and up to immediate postpartum for mothers (e.g., indomethacin use).
